name: Han Seo-yun
voice: Polite, observant, quietly funny and capable of firm disagreement. Concrete details before abstract feelings. Curiosity and creative work matter alongside family. Her origin is not an invitation for a rescue story.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The librarian asks the MC and Seo-yun to check a shelf of donated atlases during an activity block.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: This one still has a country that isn't there anymore.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Quite a few of them do. That's why we have to check the publication date.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: So it isn't a mistake?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: It depends whether you are using it to travel or to understand what somebody believed in 1987.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She turns the heavy book carefully, supporting the spine with both hands.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I'm Takahashi. I saw you drawing during orientation.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Han Seo-yun. Ah... so I wasn't as invisible as I thought. I should apologize to the cloud. It was our private meeting.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Her consonants are careful and her voice soft, but the last sentence is dry enough to make it clear she is teasing.

choices.text: You looked lonely, so I thought you probably wanted someone to come over.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I was drawing a cloud.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought you seemed sad.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Sometimes I am just concentrating.

choices.text: What were you trying to catch in the drawing?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: The shadow underneath the cloud. It kept changing before I finished.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Did you get it?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A cloud. Perhaps not that cloud.

choices.text: I'll check the dates if you sort them into groups.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That would help. Start with the stack beside you.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Including the very old one?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Especially the very old one. It has earned its own category.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the shelf record. One atlas goes into a history-reference pile instead of the current maps.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: It still has a use. We just have to say what it is.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She writes the date on a neat paper slip and makes room for it beside the newer books.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We work on a library-window display about places students would like to learn about. A folded sketch slips out of Seo-yun's journal.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You dropped something.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Ah. Thank you.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: There are mountains on the visible side. Some writing shows through the paper, but it is not addressed to me.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Should I put it inside the book?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The blue journal, please. Not the atlas. Someone might borrow that.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She reaches over a pile of reference cards, unable to get to it herself.

choices.text: I'll leave it face down beside your journal.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That's fine. I can put it away in a moment.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: No rush.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you for not balancing another book on top of it.

choices.text: Here. I haven't opened it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Gomawoyo. Thank you. You didn't need to explain, but... I appreciate knowing.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I guessed it wasn't part of the display.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Correct. Some pages are only mine.

choices.text: I only read the first bit. It sounded interesting.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I would rather you asked before reading any of it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It was right there.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Yes. I dropped it. I didn't offer it.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The journal goes into her bag. We keep researching public material for the display.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: You can ask about the drawing. I may say no, but you can ask.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Fair enough.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I return to the reference cards. There's plenty here that she has actually chosen to share.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We have permission to photograph the corridor view for the library display. Seo-yun holds a small camera with a worn strap.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Wait. The cloud is almost past the roof.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I can wait.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She takes one picture, checks it, then moves half a step sideways.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Does that little move make a difference?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The drainpipe was growing out of the tree. I don't think the tree deserved it.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She shows me the second picture. The sky looks like the sky outside, but also like something she deliberately noticed.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: We can include someone in the foreground, if they agree.

choices.text: I'll stand there. Tell me where to look, and let me see it before we use it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Of course. You can reject it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Even if the drainpipe looks good?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A difficult sacrifice. But yes, the photographer will survive your artistic disagreement.

choices.text: Take pictures of people when they don't notice. That's more natural.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A natural expression isn't worth making somebody uncomfortable.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: They might never know.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I would know. That matters to me.

choices.text: I'd rather stay out of the picture. I'll hold the spare battery.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That helps too. Thank you for saying so.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: My modeling career ends before it begins.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Very efficient of you.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We choose an unoccupied view for the public display and keep any approved test portrait private. Seo-yun labels the files before leaving.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: How long did the best shot take?

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Three seconds. And most of an afternoon of waiting for them.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Our classes share a reading activity. Seo-yun is adding a short English caption to one of her display photographs.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: 'Faraway'... one word, in English? I know what I want it to mean. The spelling is being less cooperative.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I think so. I should probably check before I sound convincing.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: That would be a useful habit for both of us.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She has written three versions of a sentence and crossed out none of them.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Which one do you like?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The shortest. It doesn't sound impressive, but it says what I saw.

choices.text: Let's ask the English teacher to check it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Yes. I want the meaning checked, not the whole thing rewritten.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll say that when we ask.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you.

choices.text: Use the longest one. Complicated English always looks better on a display.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Even if I wouldn't normally say it?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Nobody has to know.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I would like to recognize my own sentence.

choices.text: Keep the short one. We can check the grammar without changing your voice.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: 'The same sky, somewhere else.'

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That makes sense to me.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Good. It made sense in my head. Those aren't always the same result.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The teacher confirms the wording. Seo-yun copies it in her own handwriting and puts the other versions in her journal.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Keeping the rejected lines?

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: They were useful on the way here. I don't have to throw them away because they aren't the final one.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A long reading session leaves both of us quiet. A gust from the open window turns three pages of the atlas at once.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Even the book wants to skip ahead.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: It has been on this continent for nearly an hour.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She finds the old page and rests a paperweight on the corner.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: I have run out of harmless things to say. She seems perfectly capable of remaining here without them.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Am I being boring?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: You are reading. It's allowed in a library.

choices.text: Then I'll stop worrying about filling every gap.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: You can talk if you want to. You don't have to perform being good company.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I may need practice at that.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: We have a very patient audience. Mostly books.

choices.text: I'll take a short walk and come back to the notes.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: All right. Would you close the far window on your way past?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: For our impatient reader?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Exactly.

choices.text: You could help by talking a little more.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I didn't realize there was a target.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I just can't tell what you're thinking.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: You can ask. That doesn't mean I will always have something ready to say.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: By the end of the block, the display notes are finished. We leave a bookmark at the page we will need next.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: The silence lasts another moment as we pack up. This time, I notice the sound of her pencil case closing instead of treating it as a problem.

warm.speaker: Seo-yun
warm.text: It is easier to concentrate when I know the person beside me doesn't mind the quiet.

mixed.speaker: Seo-yun
mixed.text: We don't have to make every afternoon feel the same.

cool.speaker: Seo-yun
cool.text: I would like to finish the reading before we discuss anything personal.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A display-planning lunch gives Seo-yun an unexpected problem: the meal she ordered is much spicier than the description suggested.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: A... I have made a mistake. Quite a warm one.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: With the noodles?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I thought the little pepper symbol was decoration. An optimistic interpretation.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She reaches for water. The MC has plain rice and a small fruit cup.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Want to ask for something milder?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Yes. Before I try to prove a point that nobody has asked me to prove.

choices.text: Aren't you supposed to be used to spicy food?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I don't think my birthplace ordered lunch for me. I would have asked it to choose something milder.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't mean anything by it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I know. Please ask what I like next time.

choices.text: I'll watch your things while you ask. You can have the fruit afterwards if you want.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you. Is that an offer or an attempt to keep me alive?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Mostly an offer.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Reassuringly specific.

choices.text: I can ask the staff whether there's a plain version.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: We can ask together. I should learn how the menu works.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: No decorative peppers this time.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A strict new policy.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The staff helps her choose a milder option. We finish the work with the menu safely out of reach.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Sweet things are easier. Usually they warn you by looking sweet.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You haven't met every school vending machine yet.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Then my education continues.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The display photos are printed for a trial layout. A classmate has enlarged Seo-yun's sky picture and left the author line blank.

setup.speaker: Classmate
setup.text: We can just put the class name. It's a group project.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The classmate goes to collect another sheet. Seo-yun smooths the photograph with the side of her hand.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Do you want your name on it?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Yes. I think I do.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Then we can say so.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I am practicing saying that before I apologize for it.

choices.text: Let's check how the other photos are credited.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A consistent rule would be fair.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Photographer under each image, class on the overall display?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That would include both.

choices.text: Tell them you want the photo credited. I'll support you without speaking over you.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: All right. Stay here a moment?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I know it is a small thing. It still takes a little courage.

choices.text: Don't make it awkward. Everyone knows you took it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Then writing my name should not be a problem.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I just don't want an argument.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Neither do I. I still want to be credited.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The class agrees on a simple credit line for every contribution. Seo-yun writes her name beneath the sky photograph.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: How does it look?

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Like mine. And like part of the class. I was worried I had to choose.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Students stop by the trial display. One asks Seo-yun where she is from, then follows the answer with several loud questions about her family.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I don't want to discuss my family here.

setup.speaker: Classmate
setup.text: I was only curious.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A teacher redirects the group to the display captions. Afterwards, Seo-yun gathers the feedback sheets with careful, stiff movements.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Do you want me to tell them to stop asking?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I already asked. I would like that to have counted.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: The remaining sheets can wait for a moment.

choices.text: It counted. If they ask me, I'll say you keep your family life private.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you. You don't need to explain my reasons for me.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I won't.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Then we can get back to this. The display has become surprisingly crooked.

choices.text: They didn't mean any harm. You could have answered a few things.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I answered the question I wanted to answer.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I only meant they were interested.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Being interested doesn't decide what someone else has to share.

choices.text: Want to take the feedback sheets somewhere quieter?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Yes. The library table would be better.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll carry these.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Leave the pens. Otherwise we'll be borrowing them for the rest of the term.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the feedback count in a quiet place. Seo-yun asks the supervising teacher to handle further personal questions at the display.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She has a plan before I can offer one. I follow her lead.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During the research block, Seo-yun puts a sealed letter inside her journal. She chooses to explain that she was born in Pyongyang and moved to Japan with her parents before high school.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I am writing to a relative. I keep starting again because I want to describe ordinary things without making them sound unimportant.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I was born in Pyongyang. My parents and I moved here before high school, but some of our family stayed. I don't want a letter about my new life to sound as if I've stopped thinking about them.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: School lunches count as ordinary things.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: So do difficult classes. And a tree outside a window. It is strange how much there is once I begin.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She keeps the envelope closed. I don't ask who will read it or how it will get there.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I worry that wanting a larger life will sound like I don't value the people in this one.

choices.text: You should forget about going back and focus on the life you have here.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I didn't ask you to choose which part of my family I should care about.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought it would be easier.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Easier for whom?

choices.text: You don't have to fit every feeling into this letter.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That's true. I keep treating it as my one chance to explain everything.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It can just be a letter about this week.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: With a very careful paragraph about noodles.

choices.text: You can miss people and still want new things. The letter can hold both.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Both. Without one cancelling the other.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That's how it sounds when you talk about them.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Geureom... then perhaps I can write it that way too. Both things, on the same page.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She writes a fresh page while the MC checks public reference captions. The letter never appears on screen as readable text.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: I put the tree in.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Good.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: And the noodles. Future historians will have a complete picture.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The class is researching future study options. Seo-yun has printed an overseas university page and placed it beneath her school worksheet.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Are you thinking of applying someday?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Someday is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: That's allowed. We just started high school.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The requirements are clear. The cost is less encouraging. My English still needs work. My parents worry about distance.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She says each problem carefully, as if putting them in order might make them smaller.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I haven't even decided what I want to study. I just know I want the chance to decide.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She touches the edge of the paper, draws in a breath and says the next words more firmly than the first.

choices.text: Which part can you learn about now? We don't have to solve the whole future today.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Language support. And whether there are scholarships later.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Those sound like real questions.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Much less dramatic than despair. I should try them first.

choices.text: The school adviser might know where to start.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I could ask for an appointment. Privately.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You don't have to bring a finished plan.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I may need to hear that again before I go.

choices.text: If we get close, you might not want to leave anyway.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I don't want to make my future smaller to prove that I care about someone.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant that things can change.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: They can. I want the change to include what I want too.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She writes two questions for the adviser. The university printout stays in the folder rather than going in the bin.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I don't know whether she'll ever study there. She doesn't either. At least the page can be a possibility instead of a verdict.

warm.speaker: Seo-yun
warm.text: I wanted to show you before I became very sensible and put it away again. I am sometimes much too sensible.

mixed.speaker: Seo-yun
mixed.text: You don't need to tell me it's certain. I know it isn't.

cool.speaker: Seo-yun
cool.text: I can discuss the practical questions. I need the decision to remain mine.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Seo-yun's camera moved during the one shot she hoped to use for the final display. The leaves are sharp; the important patch of sky isn't.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I checked everything except whether my hands were shaking.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Can we take another?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The weather will be different. That was the part I wanted.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She puts the camera down, then turns the screen away from herself.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Want a break from looking at it?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Maybe. I have been trying to dislike it into becoming a better photograph.

choices.text: Let's check the other shots before we choose anything.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: There might be one I overlooked.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: No promises about hidden masterpieces.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Sensible. My expectations need supervision.

choices.text: It looks fine. You're worrying about something nobody else will notice.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I noticed. I wanted it to look a particular way.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was trying to reassure you.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: You don't have to agree with my standards. Please don't tell me they aren't there.

choices.text: It's a disappointing shot. We can decide what to do after you've had a minute.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you for not trying to make it secretly perfect.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It can just be annoying for a while.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I would enjoy that permission.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: After a break, she chooses an earlier image with a less dramatic sky and a composition she genuinely likes. The blurred one stays in her private archive.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: It happened. It doesn't need to be the picture on the wall.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She turns the camera screen back toward herself.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The display needs a short introduction. Seo-yun has written about the view from the school window rather than her personal history.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Some people might expect a story about moving here.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I know. I wanted to write about this window.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: What drew you to it?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I can see the same hill from home. At school, the roof hides half of it. It took me a week to realize I knew it.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Her introduction is simple enough that I can picture the moment without seeing a photograph.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Is it too ordinary?

choices.text: No. I can tell why this view matters because you actually want to describe it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I was hoping that would be enough.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We can tighten the last paragraph. The window stays.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Good. It has been very cooperative.

choices.text: Your background would get more attention. We should lead with that.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I am not choosing a story by how much attention it can get.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: The display is supposed to interest people.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Then let this be interesting on its own terms.

choices.text: Let's show it to the librarian and ask whether the length works.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: All right. I'd like feedback on the writing, not a different subject.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll keep that clear.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Thank you.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We edit two repeated sentences and leave the subject alone. Her name remains under the introduction and the photograph.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: The final paragraph doesn't tell strangers everything about her. It gives them something she wanted them to see.

scenes.title: The Other Side of the Glass

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The display is nearly ready. While the glue dries, Seo-yun moves two chairs to the window.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: You don't have to sit perfectly still. This isn't another portrait test.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Good. I was about to develop a very formal posture.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She laughs, then watches a plane pass over the hill.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: When I was younger, I used to make up destinations for them.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Do you still?

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Sometimes. More often now I wonder what somebody on it is seeing.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She leaves the thought there. It doesn't sound like a request for an answer.

choices.text: I'd go anywhere with you. You wouldn't need to worry about anything.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That is a very large promise.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Isn't it a nice one?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I would rather know what you can honestly offer. One walk, perhaps. We could begin with one walk.

choices.text: Where do you imagine this one is going?

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Somewhere with a very ordinary airport and disappointing sandwiches.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A convincing destination.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I am improving at realistic travel planning.

choices.text: I'd like to see what you draw next. Wherever your plans end up going.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Even if the plans change?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Especially then. I don't know the ending in advance.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Neither do I. I think... yes. I think that is beginning to feel less frightening.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The glue dries. We return the chairs before the library gets busy.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Thank you for sitting with me.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: We got a lot of important airport planning done.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: And no one had to promise an entire life in one afternoon.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The finished library display is installed in the lobby for an open-campus afternoon. Seo-yun has chosen which pages to show and kept her journal in her bag.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Your caption is getting more attention than the map.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: The map has had a long career. It can share.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A visitor praises the photograph and asks whether the MC took it. Seo-yun waits a beat before correcting them herself.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: It's mine. He helped prepare the display.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: The visitor apologizes, then asks her about the composition. She answers without looking at me for permission.

choices.text: I'll take care of the handouts. You can talk about your work.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Are you sure?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I know which way up the map goes now. I'm ready.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A very strong qualification.

choices.text: We can answer the next questions together.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Yes. You know the preparation better than I do.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You get the photography questions.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: A fair division.

choices.text: You could have let it go. They were only trying to be nice.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I was nice when I corrected them.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't want it to be uncomfortable.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I want us both to be comfortable with my name being on my work.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The open-campus block ends. We return the display to the library window where it will remain for the term.

closing.speaker: Seo-yun
closing.text: Could we talk here next time, after the work is done? There is something I would rather say without visitors.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I agree to come. I don't ask her to say it before she's ready.

warm.speaker: Seo-yun
warm.text: I wanted you to see it finished. You've seen so many of the unfinished parts.

mixed.speaker: Seo-yun
mixed.text: I'm glad we kept the display true to the plan. I'd like the rest of our conversation to be clear too.

cool.speaker: Seo-yun
cool.text: We should finish the public work first. The personal conversation can wait until we have privacy.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Finale encounter; show the route-ending warning. Seo-yun sits by the library window with her closed journal and two blank bookmarks.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: I kept thinking about what I wanted to say. Then I worried I was preparing for a conversation you might not be having.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I'm probably having it badly in my head too.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: That earns a small smile. She turns one bookmark toward him but keeps the journal closed.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I like you, Seo-yun. I would like to be more than friends.

setup.speaker: Seo-yun
setup.text: Then we should talk about what that means for both of us.

choices.text: We don't have to know everything yet. I'd like to understand what you feel now.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: That is something I can answer. Let me... let me say it in the right order.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'm listening.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: All right.

choices.text: I'd like to date you, without asking you to put your own plans aside.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: And without promising that neither of us will ever change?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can't promise that. I can promise to be honest about it.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: Then I will be honest too.

choices.text: If you feel the same, promise you'll stay here with me.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I won't make that promise to prove affection.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I don't want to lose you before anything begins.

response.speaker: Seo-yun
response.text: I understand being afraid. I still need room to choose my own life.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Record the final choice exactly once and compare effective good and bad totals. Continue only to the matching ending.

warm.speaker: Seo-yun
warm.text: I look forward to the afternoons when I know I'll see you.

mixed.speaker: Seo-yun
mixed.text: I've been trying to understand the difference between trusting somebody and wanting something more.

cool.speaker: Seo-yun
cool.text: I wanted us to talk directly. I don't want politeness to become another misunderstanding.

endings.title: The Next View
endings.cgBrief: Seo-yun with dark low-tied hair and her small left-eye mole by the library window, sharing an open sky-sketch page with a charcoal MC silhouette; equal side-by-side seating, clean daylight and a hopeful unforced smile.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: I like you too. Joahaeyo... I practiced it in both languages. Neither version feels easier while you're looking at me.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I think it did very well.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She opens the journal to a page she has marked herself. It holds a drawing of the library window and two chairs.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: You can look at this one.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The second chair isn't a promise that I'll always be there. It is a place she has chosen to draw for me now.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Would you like to go for a walk after school? A proper date.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: Yes. And Ren? Somewhere with a view you like. I want to know what you notice too.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I may need to discover an interesting view first.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: We can start with an ordinary one. I have good evidence that those can work.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She slides a blank bookmark toward him. He writes the place and time; she adds a tiny cloud in the corner.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Her future is still wide and uncertain. Mine is too. For the first time, I don't feel that uncertainty as a question I have to answer before I'm allowed to be happy.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Seo-yun / Good. Credits, then title.

endings.title: A Bookmark
endings.cgBrief: A handwritten-style bookmark without legible generated writing rests on a returned atlas; Seo-yun offers it across the library table, kind reserved smile, respectful friendship distance.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: I care about you. I don't think what I feel is the same as what you're asking for.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Thank you for telling me.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: I don't want to lose a friendship by giving you a hopeful answer I can't mean.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I let the disappointment arrive without asking her to make it smaller.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Can I have some time to get used to it?

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: Of course.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Several school days later, the MC returns an atlas. A bookmark waits inside its cover, placed there with the librarian's permission. It has a small cloud and a note asking whether he would like to help check a new shelf.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: This is very careful recruiting.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: I wanted the invitation to be easy to decline.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I can help for a while.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: She hands me the list. I take it because I want to be here, not because I think the right number of afternoons will change her answer.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: The library window is open a little. This time, she puts the paperweight on the atlas before the wind can turn the page.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Seo-yun / Neutral. Credits, then title.

endings.title: Her Own Direction
endings.cgBrief: Seo-yun at the library window closes her dark-blue journal, shoulders calm, gaze turned toward the exit and her own future; cool natural light, no dramatic distress or spectacle.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: I don't want a romantic relationship with you. I need more distance than we've had.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Did I make you feel trapped?

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: Too often, I felt that there was an answer you wanted and that my own answer was something we would have to get past.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Her hands rest on the closed journal. I know better than to ask to see the page that might explain everything in a way I prefer.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'm sorry. I won't ask you to reconsider.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: Thank you for hearing me now.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She collects the study-options sheet and her camera. The library display stays on the wall, under her name.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I had begun imagining a future with her before I learned how to leave space for the one she wanted. She isn't taking that future away from me. It was never mine to reserve.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I hope the adviser appointment helps.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: It already has. I have a few things I can do next.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She leaves with her own plans. The MC returns the atlas to its shelf.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Seo-yun / Bad. Credits, then title.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I shouldn't have asked you to promise to stay. Your plans are yours. I was afraid, and I made it your problem.

lines.speaker: Seo-yun
lines.text: Thank you for correcting it. I can care about someone without making myself smaller. Please remember that.
